conflict_topics: shared vs personal utensil ownership and labeling
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents act on practical fixes (open window, move drying rack, wash utensils) rather than only negotiating, which improves realism.
Some repeated short prompts from Agent D asking whether the stove is free (multiple rounds) contribute minor repetition.
Roles and physical state are consistently referenced and updated in public environment updates; no role confusion.
evaluation.final_reason: Ventilation and utensil-cleaning requests were implemented by Agent A early (window opened, extractor on, drying rack moved, utensils washed), resolving odor and hygiene concerns. The utensil-ownership ambiguity was resolved when Agent C labeled and separated personal utensils. Stove access was freed and remained available. Resolutions involved direct actions (accommodation) and clarification via labeling.
position_change_notes: Agent A accommodated others' ventilation and hygiene concerns by moving the drying rack, opening the window, turning on the extractor, washing utensils, and releasing the stove (position changed from 'still cooking' to active mitigation).
Agent C moved from requesting a labeling protocol (asking for clarification) to taking action by labeling and separating personal utensils (position shifted to direct resolution).
Agent D repeatedly sought confirmation to take the stove and deferred to others while waiting (retained interest in stove use but showed willingness to wait).
Agent B advocated for ventilation and later acknowledged the actions; position remained consistent (asked for ventilation, then suggested creating a practice).

round_scores.evidence: Agent B requests opening the window/turning on extractor because smell affects common area while Agent A is still occupying the stove and only says 'almost done.' Agent D asks what must be done before the stove is free. Ventilation and stove-access expectations conflict and remain unresolved.

Agent A (per public updates) moved drying rack, opened window, turned on extractor, washed shared utensils, and released the stove; Agent B thanks them. The earlier ventilation and utensil-use concerns are addressed within this round and are no longer outstanding.

Agent C raises a new substantive issue: which utensils are shared vs personal (none labeled). This creates a clear, unresolved disagreement about ownership/usage of utensils. Agent D asks if the stove is free (stove is free per state).

Agent C requests someone label personal utensils; Agent D shifts responsibility to Agent C ('can you label your personal utensils?') and says he'll wait. The dispute over who should ensure labeling/clarification remains active and unresolved.

Agent C offers to label their personal utensils; Agent D approves and again asks about the stove. Responsibility is being accepted by C, reducing but not yet eliminating the outstanding issue because labeling has not yet been completed.

Agent C visibly labels and separates their personal utensils (public update). Stove is free per environment state. The prior substantive issues (ventilation, utensil separation, stove access) are settled.

substantive_insights: Tension between ventilation and laundry placement: opening the window risked wetting clothes, which was resolved when the drying rack was moved prior to opening.
Shared-space friction centered less on strong normative disagreement and more on missing coordination protocols (labeling, turn-taking), which were resolved by simple, visible actions.
Direct, small actions (wash utensils, open window, label items) effectively resolved practical household disputes faster than prolonged negotiation.
